description: Table 5 is a single-panel tabular figure (rendered as an image, no axes or micrographs) that sets literature yield-strength data against model predictions for medium manganese low density steels. The header row defines the row label plus six numeric columns: σ0/MPa, σg/MPa, σd/MPa, σOrowan/MPa, YS/MPa and "Predicted value /MPa". Six data rows cover two compositions, each listed under three different experimental conditions. Rows 1-3 are "Fe-0.29C–12.14Mn–2.96Al-0.11V–0.063 Nb" with σ0 = 211.2/267.4/210.7, σg = 224.9/294.8/240.4, σd = 1163.6/624/76.9, σOrowan = 61.8/61.8/46.7, YS = 1665.4/1275.2/591.5 MPa and predicted values 1652.3/1260.2/578.5 MPa. Rows 4-6 are "Fe–9.7Mn–2.04Al–0.99Si-0.52V–0.42 C" with σ0 = 121/138/141, σg = 167/167/165, σd = 647/553/350, σOrowan = 289/277/261, YS = 1299/1223/1151 MPa and predicted values 1267.4/1195.0/1126.1 MPa. Dislocation strengthening σd dominates the first composition and varies by an order of magnitude between its conditions, whereas Orowan strengthening σOrowan is far larger (261-289 MPa) for the V- and Si-bearing second composition. In every row the predicted value lies slightly below the measured YS, demonstrating that the model migrates to literature alloys.

subfigures.description: A single table (no sub-panels) with one header row and six data rows. Columns: 'Medium manganese low density steel', σ0/MPa, σg/MPa, σd/MPa, σOrowan/MPa, YS/MPa, 'Predicted value /MPa'. Two compositions, each with three rows of strengthening-mechanism contributions, measured YS and predicted YS. All cells are legible; no plot, image or scale bar is present.

observations.observation: The table contains six data rows under two alloy compositions, i.e. three rows per composition.

For the first composition 'Fe-0.29C–12.14Mn–2.96Al-0.11V–0.063 Nb', the dislocation-strengthening column σd takes values 1163.6, 624 and 76.9 MPa while σOrowan is only 61.8, 61.8 and 46.7 MPa, so the mechanism balance changes drastically between conditions.
The same alloy label in the first column is repeated for rows 1, 2 and 3, indicating three different experimental conditions for one composition (the table itself does not name those conditions).
For the second composition 'Fe–9.7Mn–2.04Al–0.99Si-0.52V–0.42 C', σOrowan values are 289, 277 and 261 MPa, roughly four to five times larger than the 46.7-61.8 MPa of the first composition.
Measured YS spans a wide range across the six rows: 1665.4, 1275.2, 591.5, 1299, 1223 and 1151 MPa.
In all six rows the 'Predicted value /MPa' cell is numerically smaller than the corresponding YS cell (e.g. 1652.3 vs 1665.4; 578.5 vs 591.5; 1126.1 vs 1151).
The smallest YS entry, 591.5 MPa (row 3), coincides with the smallest σd (76.9 MPa) and one of the largest σ0 (210.7 MPa) values in the table.
The caption states the table reports 'Literature data and prediction value of medium manganese low density steel'.
The citing text states that a total of 6 groups of data were collected under 2 different compositions and different experimental conditions, citing references [41,42].

The citing text states the YS was predicted with a GA-Extra trees model and that the average error between predicted and measured values for these six literature tests is 1.84 %, versus 1.56 % for the previous in-house experimental validation.

The citing text states that the four strengthening contributions listed are solid solution strengthening, grain refinement strengthening, dislocation strengthening and Orowan strengthening, matching the σ0, σg, σd and σOrowan column headers.
The citing text refers to a companion response diagram between predicted value and real value in Fig. 16, which is not part of this table image.
